texts.preamble: Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 In the Court of Dr. Satinder Kumar Gautam: Additional Sessions Judge -(03) (East) Karkardooma Courts: Delhi. Criminal Appeal No. 145/2019 Madhu Sharma W/o Sh. R.K. Sharma R/o G-2, Type Ii, Block 1, Kalyanvas, Delhi Also At D-2, Green Park, Chipyana Buzarg, I Floor, Jaat Chowk Near A.B.S.E. College, Lal Kuan, Ghaziabad Up - 201 009 ........ Appellant Vs. 1. The State Govt. of Nct of Delhi Through Secretary/Ld. App 2. Smt. Veema W/o Sh. Shankar Lal R/o H. No. 328, Kalyanvas Delhi - 110 091 ........Respondents Date of Institution : 13.09.2019 Judgment Reserved on : 22.02.2021 Date of Judgment : 24.02.2021 Crl. Appeal No. 1452019 Madhu Sharma Vs. State & Anr Page 1 of 12 Arising out of Ct 4365/2016 titled as Madhu Sharma Vs. Veena & Anr. Ps Kalyanpuri Judgment:
texts.facts: 1. Ms. Madhu Sharma, the sole appellant, after invoking the provisions of the provisions of Sec. 372 CrPC, preferred the above criminal appeal and challenges the impugned judgment/order dated 17.05.2019 passed by ld. MM whereby acquitting the accused Veena stood acquitted for the offences alleged against her. 2. It is also to be mentioned here that along with the present criminal appeal an application under Sec. 5 of Limitation Act was also filed. 3. Notice of the present criminal appeal along with the application was issued to the respondents. 5. Qua application on condonation of delay, ld. counsel prayed for condoning the delay of around 85 days on various ground stating that firstly, appellant is an old lady and fully dependent on her husband for financial assistance and later on suffered with eye problem and when contacted her counsel, mother of counsel expired and then appeal was filed with such a delay period. 7. Respondent no. 2 hotly contested the present criminal appeal and application under Sec. 5 of Limitation Act on all grounds.
texts.arguments: 6. On merits of the present criminal appeal, it is contended by ld. counsel for the appellant that the impugned judgment/order suffers from patent illegality, perversity, arbitrary and even not sustainable in the eyes of law further contending that same has been passed without considering the entire facts and material on record. One of the contentions of the ld. counsel for the appellant is that judgment dated 17.05.2019 is totally based on surmises and conjectures and hence prayed for setting aside of the same. His first contention is that even the present criminal appeal is not maintainable as the victim has no right to prefer the present appeal before the Court of Sessions and has only remedy to prefer the appeal before Hon'ble High Court after taking Leave and as such, prayed for dismissal of the present criminal appeal only on this count. Countering the said arguments, ld. counsel for the appellant placed reliance on the cases reported as S. Ganapathy Vs. N. Senthilvel [Crl. A (MD) No. 99 of 2015] decided on 05.04.2016 by Hon'ble High Court of Madras urging that present criminal appeal is maintainable. It is further contended by ld. counsel for the appellant that present criminal appeal be allowed and impugned order/judgment dated 17.05.2019 be [LEAKAGE_MASK] after condoning the delay in preferring the present criminal appeal. In case reported as AIR 2014 SC 746 titled as Basawaraj & Anr. Vs The Spl. Land Acquisition Officer, Hon'ble Apex Court observed as - Condonation of delay without considering the most relevant factor i.e. "sufficient cause" only on the condition that applicant would be deprived of interest for the delay period is most in appropriate. 15. In a case reported as The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. Vs. Sushil Kumar, Crl. A. No. 972/2012 decided on 03.09.2014. in its paras 13 to 16 Hon'ble court observed as: "In my considered view, the "complaint" in the proceedings under Sec. 138 N.I. Act cannot be considered "victim" in the letter and spirit of the definition of Sec. 2 (wa) of the Code and definition of "injury" under Section 44 IPC cannot be imported into Sec. 138 N.I. Act. The controversy now is no longer res integra in view of the pronouncement of law by Supreme Court in "Subhash Chand Vs. State (Delhi Administration).(2013) 2 SCC 17. It was a complaint case under Sec. 7 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, in which Subhash Chand was tried and he was acquitted by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate. The State filed criminal appeal before the Sessions Court under Sec. 378 (1) (a) CrPC. But once it is a case instituted on a Madhu Sharma vs The State on 24 February, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153084365/ 4 complaint and an order of acquittal is passed, whether the offence is bailable, non-bailable, cognizable or non- cognizable, the complainant can file an application under Sc. 378 (4) for special leave to appeal against it in the High Court. Section 378 (4) places no restriction on the complainant..." 17. In another case reported as Bhavuben Dineshbhai Makwana V. State of Gujarat & Ors 2013 Crl LJ 4225, Full Bench of Gujarat High Court answering the reference on question number (3) "if the victim prefers an appeal before this court, challenging the acquittal, invoking his right under proviso to section 372 of CrPC, whether that appellant is required to first seek leave of the Court, as is required in case of appeal being preferred by the State?, held - "if the victim also happens to be the complainant and the appeal is against the acquittal, he is required to take leave as provided in Sec. 378 of the Criminal Procedure Code but if he is not the complainant, he is not required to apply for or obtain any leave. For the appeal against inadequency of compensation or punishment on a lesser offence, no leave is necessary at the instance of a victim, whether he is the complainant or not." 18. In case reported as Subhash Chand (supra), Hon'ble Apex Court observed as - "...In view of the above, we conclude that a complainant can file an application for special leave to appeal against an order of acquittal of any kind only to the High Court. The appellant was acquitted by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi.
